symbols.description: A narrow band of strong wind and a type of air current that forms high in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: Jet stream

symbols.description: The four main jet streams associated with Earth: two polar jet streams and two subtropical jet streams.
symbols.name: Primary jet streams

symbols.description: A jet stream near one of Earth’s poles; polar jet streams can reach especially high speeds in winter.
symbols.name: Polar jet stream

symbols.description: A jet stream located closer to the equator.
symbols.name: Subtropical jet stream

symbols.description: Moving air, including the strong movement found in jet streams.
symbols.name: Wind

symbols.description: A movement of air; a jet stream is a type of air current.
symbols.name: Air current

symbols.description: A mass of warmer air that meets cooler air masses and rises higher in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: Warm air mass

symbols.description: A mass of cooler air that meets warmer air masses and sinks to replace rising warm air.
symbols.name: Cool air mass

symbols.description: The layer of air surrounding Earth in which jet streams form and in which air masses move.
symbols.name: Atmosphere

symbols.description: The planet whose atmosphere, surface, poles, equator, and jet streams are described.
symbols.name: Earth

symbols.description: The source of heating that does not warm the whole Earth evenly.
symbols.name: Sun

symbols.description: The region of Earth near which areas are hot and subtropical jet streams are located closer.
symbols.name: Equator

symbols.description: The north and south polar regions of Earth, near which areas are cold and polar jet streams are located.
symbols.name: Poles

symbols.description: The upward movement of warmer air in the atmosphere when it meets cooler air.
symbols.name: Warm-air rise

symbols.description: The downward movement of cooler air to replace warmer air that has risen.
symbols.name: Cool-air sinking

aliases: warm air masses meet cold air masses
symbols.description: The meeting of warm and cool air masses that forms jet streams and can create turbulent conditions.
symbols.name: Air-mass meeting

symbols.description: The formation of a jet stream when warm air masses meet cold air masses in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: Jet-stream formation

symbols.description: The speed at which a jet stream moves, averaging about 110 miles per hour and sometimes reaching 250 miles per hour or faster.
symbols.name: Jet-stream speed

symbols.description: The direction in which a jet stream travels or moves, generally from west to east but sometimes in different ways.
symbols.name: Jet-stream direction

symbols.description: The position of a jet stream about five to nine miles above Earth’s surface in the mid to upper troposphere.
symbols.name: Jet-stream location

symbols.description: The layer of Earth’s atmosphere where people live and breathe, including its mid to upper region where jet streams and airplanes are located.
symbols.name: Troposphere

symbols.description: An aircraft that flies in the mid to upper troposphere and can receive a boost from a jet stream when traveling in the same direction.
symbols.name: Airplane

symbols.description: An increase in an airplane’s travel advantage when it flies in the same direction as a powerful jet stream.
symbols.name: Airplane boost

symbols.description: A system of weather that jet streams can transport across the United States or that can remain in place when far from a jet stream.
symbols.name: Weather system

symbols.description: The region across which jet streams can transport weather systems.
symbols.name: United States

symbols.description: A property of air and weather that differs between warm and cool air masses and is affected by jet streams.
symbols.name: Temperature

symbols.description: A weather condition affected by weather systems transported by jet streams.
symbols.name: Precipitation

symbols.description: A period of heat that can result when a weather system remains in one place away from a jet stream.
symbols.name: Heat wave

symbols.description: A condition that can result when a weather system remains in one place away from a jet stream.
symbols.name: Flood

symbols.description: A weather event that jet streams typically move and that tends to follow the edge of a jet stream.
symbols.name: Storm

symbols.description: A bulge of winds to the north or south created when a jet stream moves in a different way from its usual west-to-east travel.
symbols.name: Jet-stream bulge

symbols.description: The edge of a jet stream that storms tend to follow.
symbols.name: Jet-stream edge

symbols.description: Conditions created where the difference between cool and warm air near the edge of a jet stream contributes to storms.
symbols.name: Turbulent conditions

symbols.description: Cold air that meets warmer and wetter air when a jet stream is pushed farther south.
symbols.name: Arctic air

symbols.description: An atmospheric phenomenon associated with the warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a southward-pushed jet stream.
symbols.name: Thunder

symbols.description: An atmospheric phenomenon associated with the warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a southward-pushed jet stream.
symbols.name: Lightning

symbols.description: A severe weather event associated with the warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a southward-pushed jet stream.
symbols.name: Tornado
